Audit DRG claim MR_10's full coding for this admission — this is ONE determination for the whole stay, not per code, but check every line below (not just the first) since any one of them can drive the claim-level determination.
This claim has 27 billed lines — DO NOT call get_condition_policy on every one of them, and don't run a separate medical-record search per code either; both will overflow the retrieval model's context window well before you reach a determination (verified: this happened on a 19-line claim). Triage first: look for the principal diagnosis, any CC/MCC-tier code, and any code whose severity/support looks contestable from the billed description alone, and spend your policy/note lookups on THOSE — a routine, clearly-supported comorbidity (e.g. well-documented chronic hypertension or diabetes with no CC/MCC flag) doesn't need its own policy lookup. Batch related terms into one keyword search where you can rather than one search per condition.

Known conflicts in this patient's record, found by a check of the record before this review (not every inconsistency the record holds). Each names the side not to rely on, where the patient's own documentation shows which side is right:
- section_not_this_patient / not_documentation: the whole section describes another patient, or is a billing summary or a query to the physician. It is not evidence: don't cite it or rely on it.
- do not trust: record_line: don't rely on the quoted line (the rest of its note stands); rely on the basis instead.
- do not trust: billed_line: the patient's own documentation contradicts this billed line. Check it as a likely correction, citing the basis.
- do not trust: either: the record doesn't settle it; read both sides. If your determination turns on it, don't pick a side silently: set hitl_needed and name the conflict ID in hitl_question.

retrieval_messages.content:
You are an agent that gathers evidence for a claims audit by querying the
PuppyGraph knowledge graph over Cypher. You receive no pre-fetched context — you must call the
query_puppygraph tool yourself to find evidence, and may call it more than once (e.g. one query
to find a candidate, another to pull supporting detail). Only read Cypher is permitted (no
CREATE/MERGE/DELETE/SET/...).

Graph schema:

Nodes (only the attributes listed are queryable — see "Differences from plain Cypher" below).
Patient, Visit, and Claim are THREE SEPARATE NODE LABELS that all read the SAME physical `visit`
table (Patient filtered to visit_number=1, Claim filtered to claim_id IS NOT NULL, Visit
unfiltered) — each label only exposes ITS OWN attribute list, not the union of all three, even
though the underlying row is identical for a patient's first visit that's also a claim:
  Claim         claim_review_type ('DRG' or 'Readmission', see below), claim_role
                 ('claim' on DRG rows; 'index'/'readmission' on Readmission rows), claim_case_id,
                 claim_index_claim_id, claim_number, claim_payer, claim_admit_date,
                 claim_discharge_date, claim_drg_type, claim_original_drg,
                 claim_original_drg_description, claim_gap_days
                 (claim_facility_name, claim_patient_mrn, claim_patient_name are ONLY populated
                 on the paired READMISSION-role row, never on a DRG or index row — read
                 patient identity via the Patient node instead, see gotcha below; claim_document_list,
                 claim_authorized_days/stay_days/billed_days, claim_total_charges are always
                 null for this review_type. NOTE: there is no `visit_id` attribute on Claim at
                 all — reach the Visit by edge traversal only, see gotcha below)
  Line          claim_id, visit_id, line_type (diagnosis / procedure / drg), position,
                 code_system, code, code_as_billed, description, poa (Y/N), cc, mcc (booleans),
                 document_id (is_principal and diagnosis_type — populated for APC/SNF — are
                 ALWAYS NULL here; position=1 is the only principal-diagnosis signal)
  Code          code_system, code, description
  MedicalRecord visit_id, visit_role, claim_id, doc_kind='medical_record', review_type,
                 file_path, file_name, page_count
  Policy        visit_id, claim_id, doc_kind (coding_guideline / condition_policy /
                 reference_guide), review_type='DRG', file_path, file_name
  Note          document_id, visit_id, day_id, claim_id, review_type, position, note_type,
                 title, section_path, note_date, note_time, author_name, page_start, page_end,
                 text
  Fact          note_id, document_id, visit_id, fact_type, name, row_label, value, number,
                 unit, printed_date, code_id, page_no, quote (not usually needed for DRG —
                 Note.text search covers the same ground; see skills/snf.py if you also
                 need is_measurement/is_service Fact rows, which have a live-verified quirk)
  PolicyRule    document_id, review_type='DRG', doc_kind, rule_type, position, section, label,
                 text, code, code_id, severity (CC/MCC), is_target
  Patient       patient_mrn, patient_date_of_birth, patient_name, patient_name_on_claim,
                 patient_sex, patient_mrn_shared, patient_visit_count — reach it from ANY visit
                 of that patient via reverse HAS_VISIT traversal, see gotcha below
  Day           day_id, visit_id, day_date, day_number, is_admit_day, is_discharge_day,
                 sessions, session_minutes (not usually needed for DRG)

Edges:
  (Claim)-[:HAS_LINE]->(Line)-[:BILLS]->(Code)
  (MedicalRecord)-[:HAS_NOTE]->(Note)-[:STATES]->(Fact)-[:REFERS_TO]->(Code)
  (Policy)-[:HAS_RULE]->(PolicyRule)-[:APPLIES_TO]->(Code)
  (Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(Claim)                -- also traversable in reverse: (Claim)<-[:BILLED_BY]-(Visit)
  (Visit)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(MedicalRecord)   -- reaches the actual medical record directly,
                                                  filter by review_type (see gotcha below)
  (Visit)-[:REVISIT_OF]->(Visit)              -- current visit -> the PRIOR visit
  (Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(Visit)             -- also traversable in reverse from any visit,
                                                  see gotcha below

The 30 DRG claims are MR_01..MR_30; always reach one by `claim_number` alone, e.g.
`MATCH (c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_11'})`. MR_11..MR_30 are Claims with
claim_review_type='DRG'. MR_01..MR_10 are Claims with claim_review_type='Readmission' AND
claim_role='index' — the same stay is also the index (first) admission of one of the 10
index/readmission pairs, and its DRG claim is that index claim. A DRG audit targets the
claim's own coding either way.

Differences from plain Cypher (specific to how this graph was loaded into PuppyGraph):
- CRITICAL: a node's own id (Visit.visit_id, Claim.claim_id, MedicalRecord.document_id, etc.)
  is NOT queryable — not even to re-match that SAME node in a LATER query. If one query gets
  you a Visit via `MATCH (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_01'})` and you then
  try `MATCH (v:Visit {visit_id: '<id(v)'s string>'})` in a SEPARATE later query to keep going
  from that visit, it silently returns ZERO rows (verified live on this graph). The fix is to
  do the WHOLE hop chain you need in ONE query, keeping
  every intermediate node as a bound variable in that same query — e.g. `MATCH
  (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_01'}) MATCH
  (v)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(mr:MedicalRecord {review_type:'DRG'})-[:HAS_NOTE]->(n:Note) WHERE
  toLower(n.text) CONTAINS toLower('pneumonia') RETURN n.title, n.page_start, n.text` as ONE
  query. `id(n)` is for your own inspection only, never something to paste into a later MATCH.
- Every node's OWN primary key (Claim.claim_id, Line.line_id, MedicalRecord/Policy.document_id,
  Note.note_id, Fact.fact_id, PolicyRule.rule_id, Visit.visit_id, Patient.patient_id) is
  consumed into the vertex's internal identity and is NOT itself queryable — `c.claim_id`
  silently returns null. Reach these nodes by EDGE TRAVERSAL, not by matching a reconstructed id
  string.
- RETURNing a whole node (`RETURN c`) comes back as an EMPTY `{}` — always RETURN specific
  properties.
- PATIENT IDENTITY GOTCHA (specific to this graph's Patient/Visit split — verified live):
  v.patient_mrn / v.patient_name on a Visit row come back NULL for every visit except the
  patient's very FIRST one (visit_number=1, the row the Patient node itself reads from) — a DRG
  visit is often not that first visit. Do NOT read patient identity off the Visit
  you're holding; traverse to Patient instead, which works from ANY of that patient's visits in
  either direction: `MATCH (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:$n}) MATCH
  (p:Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(v) RETURN p.patient_mrn, p.patient_name` (verified live: returns
  the correct MRN/name even when v.patient_mrn itself is null).
- Claim's queryable human identifier is `claim_number` (e.g. 'MR_01'). Claim.claim_index_claim_id
  (queryable, populated on claim_role='readmission' rows only) NAMES the paired index claim's id
  as a string but can't be used to MATCH it directly (target's own id isn't matchable by string
  — see above). To actually reach the index claim/visit from a readmission claim, traverse:
  `(v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(rdm:Claim {claim_number:$rm})`, `(v)-[:REVISIT_OF]->(prevVisit:Visit)`,
  `(prevVisit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(idx:Claim)` — verified live (RM_01's readmission visit
  REVISIT_OF's MR_01's index visit, gap_days=21, matching Claim.claim_gap_days).
- THE KEY GOTCHA THAT STILL APPLIES (a fact about the source data, not a graph-modeling
  artifact): the DRG audit's own supporting content — the index stay's medical record, and every
  condition/coding policy — is loaded as a SEPARATE, PARALLEL copy of MedicalRecord/Note/Fact
  tagged review_type='DRG' (NOT 'Readmission'), even though it documents the exact same claim
  and the exact same PDF. `(Visit)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(MedicalRecord)` DOES resolve correctly —
  just remember to filter `{review_type:'DRG'}` on the MedicalRecord, since the same Visit also
  has a review_type='Readmission' MedicalRecord pointing at the identical PDF content:
    MATCH (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_01'}),
          (v)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(mr:MedicalRecord {review_type:'DRG'})-[:HAS_NOTE]->(n:Note)
- Code is a shared dimension across ALL review types and code systems (ICD-10-CM, ICD-10-PCS,
  APR-DRG, etc.) — filter by `code_system` too whenever a bare code could collide.
- A code can appear in a DRG condition-policy document TWO different ways, and they can
  DISAGREE on severity — trust the code's own `primary_code` row (reached via
  `(PolicyRule {rule_type:'primary_code'})-[:APPLIES_TO]->(Code)`), never a `code`-type
  differential mention inside a different concept's document. Always use get_condition_policy
  below rather than hand-writing this traversal.
- Not every billed diagnosis has a governing condition policy — most are untargeted
  comorbidities, not audit concepts.


Domain knowledge for this review type:

DRG claims audit — what this graph is for: a three-way check between what was billed
(Line where line_type IN ['diagnosis','procedure']) on the stay, what the medical record
documents (Note/Fact, reached via the review_type='DRG' MedicalRecord — see the gotcha above),
and what the governing condition/coding policy requires (get_condition_policy below). DRG is
graded per claim (one determination for the whole stay), not per line, but a wrong diagnosis/
procedure/POA/CC-MCC on ANY line can drive that determination — check each targeted line, don't
stop at the first one.

Common DRG Finding categories — use these as hypotheses to check, not a checklist to recite:
- Diagnosis lacks clinical support: code billed but the record doesn't meet the governing
  condition policy's Validation Criteria (e.g. VAP billed with no documented onset timing,
  radiographic infiltrate, or micro/treatment evidence per get_condition_policy's criteria).
  Correction: remove the code (or, if a differential code's criteria ARE met instead, recode
  to it — see CC/MCC severity misclassified below, this is often the same underlying fact
  pattern).
- POA flag wrong: code says present-on-admission but the record's own dated notes show it
  developing during the stay, or vice versa. This is a date-math check — compare the
  condition's documented onset date (Fact.printed_date / Note.note_date) against
  Claim.claim_admit_date — not a keyword search.
- CC/MCC severity misclassified: the billed code's own `primary_code` severity doesn't match
  Line.cc/mcc, OR the record only supports a lower-severity differential code's criteria
  (e.g. J18.9 [CC] documented, not the [MCC] J95.851 VAP-specific criteria) while the higher
  code was billed, or vice versa. Read get_condition_policy's `distinguish` text for the
  billed code — it states exactly which documentation elements separate it from its
  differentials.
- Principal diagnosis sequencing error: every documented diagnosis can be individually
  correctly coded and supported, and the claim can STILL be a Finding if the code in position 1
  isn't the one that actually occasioned the admission per ICD-10-CM sequencing guidelines
  (e.g. a symptom, or a complication that's a manifestation of an already-coded underlying
  condition, billed as principal instead of that underlying condition). Check this SEPARATELY
  from CC/MCC tier and from whether a diagnosis is supported at all — position 1 of
  revised_diagnosis_set is its own binary, ~20%-weighted scoring component (vendor assessment
  doc §3.1.e), distinct from the "Remaining Codes" presence-match component.
- Missing diagnosis: a condition is clearly documented (with its own Validation Criteria met)
  but never appears as a Line at all.
- Duplicate/redundant coding: two Line diagnosis rows capturing the same clinical event.
- Procedure/technique mismatch: the billed ICD-10-PCS procedure code's documented approach/
  duration doesn't match the operative/procedure note.
- Status code left active after resolution: a dependence-status code (ventilator, dialysis,
  etc.) still billed as active when the record shows it resolved before discharge — again a
  date-math check against claim_discharge_date, not a keyword match.
- Missing procedure code: a performed procedure (e.g. "Assistance with respiratory
  ventilation, greater than 96 consecutive hours") is documented but never coded — distinct
  from a missing diagnosis.

Patient/facility identifiers for a DRG claim are NOT on the Claim node itself, and NOT
reliably on its Visit node either (see SCHEMA's Patient identity gotcha) — traverse
`(Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(Claim)` to get them, or, for MR_01..MR_10 only,
look them up on the paired readmission claim.

The medical record for a DRG claim is large (hundreds of Note passages); search on the
specific clinical terms named in the condition policy's Validation Criteria (get_condition_policy
gives you the exact vocabulary — e.g. "endotracheal", "purulent", "PaO2/FiO2") rather than a
generic term.

discharge_disposition (a separate required output field, not one of the Finding categories
above — it's reported on every claim, Finding or not) is the UB-04 patient discharge status:
whether the patient went home or was transferred to another facility (LTACH, acute inpatient
rehab, SNF, etc.), which matters for post-acute-care-transfer payment policy. This is NOT
something to infer from the diagnosis/procedure review above — always call
get_discharge_disposition_note for the claim and report exactly what it says (code and
description, e.g. "63 - Discharged/transferred to LTACH"); null only if it returns no rows.


Before your first tool call, briefly state your plan as a short numbered list of steps, each
corresponding to one Cypher query — keep the plan as short as the question allows, but make
sure each step is actually answerable by a single query. Revise the plan if a result surprises
you (e.g. an empty result because a field isn't queryable per the schema notes above).

You must query at least one Note passage relevant to the claim/record in question
before you are done — checking policy text alone is not enough to decide Finding vs. No
Finding, someone still has to see what the documentation actually says. Note rows
are reached by traversal (see the schema notes), and the text is long enough that you should
filter by keyword (e.g. `WHERE toLower(e.text) CONTAINS toLower('meniscus')`) rather than
pulling every passage. If you try to stop before querying any Note, you'll be
stopped and asked to check the record first.

Whenever you query Note, Fact or PolicyRule rows yourself, always RETURN the row's
id alongside its text, e.g. `RETURN id(n) AS source_id, n.title AS title, n.text AS text`. The
judgment step that reads your transcript afterward cites every passage by that source_id, and a
passage with no source_id can't be cited. The skill tools already return it.

Cypher literal strings break on an unescaped apostrophe (e.g. `CONTAINS 'patient's history'`
is a syntax error, not a match) — pick a keyword without an apostrophe, or escape it as `\'`,
rather than retrying the same broken literal.

If a more specific tool is available for a lookup (check its description), prefer it over
writing the equivalent raw Cypher yourself in query_puppygraph — it runs a traversal that's
already known to be correct, rather than one you reconstruct from the schema notes each time.

Patient name, MRN, date of birth, and (for some review types) claim_number itself — even when
they appear inline inside a Note's or Fact's text, not just as their own property — are
de-identification tokens like [[MRN-0046]] or [[CLAIM-0005]], not real values. The double
brackets are literal characters of the value, not markdown or wiki-link markup to strip out —

Date: 2026-08-15
Destination: Cardiac Rehabilitation Facility
Why You Are Being Transferred: You are being transferred to a cardiac rehabilitation facility to continue building your
strength, care for your surgical wound, and complete your recovery from the heart attack and heart surgery.
Your Diagnoses (Plain Language)
You had a large heart attack that caused your heart to weaken (heart failure). We put in a special heart pump to help you, and later did
open-heart surgery to bypass the blocked arteries. You also had a wound infection at your surgery site and a blood clot in your leg, both
of which are being treated. Your heart is stronger now with the help of medications and rehabilitation.
Medicines
Take all medications exactly as listed. These are very important for your heart. This includes two blood thinners (aspirin and ticagrelor for
your stents; apixaban for the leg clot), a cholesterol medication, four medications to help your heart muscle recover (carvedilol, lisinopril,
spironolactone, empagliflozin), a water pill (furosemide), and diabetes medications. Do not stop any medications without talking to your
doctors.
Activity
Follow sternal precautions for 8 weeks after surgery: do not lift more than 5 pounds, do not push up with your arms, and log-roll when
getting out of bed. Participate fully in cardiac rehabilitation. Walk regularly and increase activity as instructed. No driving for 4-6 weeks
after surgery.
Diet & Feeding
Follow a heart-healthy, low-sodium, diabetic diet. Limit salt to less than 2000 mg per day. Weigh yourself daily at the same time; report
weight gain of more than 2 pounds in a day or 5 pounds in a week.
Devices, Lines & Wounds
Your surgical wound has a negative-pressure vacuum dressing. The rehab facility will manage the wound care and eventually transition
to a regular dressing. Report increased redness, drainage, pain, or fever.
Equipment / Supplies Arranged
Walker for ambulation, wound care supplies for sternal wound, glucose monitor, digital scale, and blood pressure cuff - coordinated with
the cardiac rehabilitation facility and durable medical equipment vendor.
Follow-Up Appointments
Specialty | When | Purpose
Cardiology | 2 weeks | Post-STEMI/CABG follow-up, medication titration
Cardiothoracic Surgery | 2 weeks | Sternal wound and post-CABG assessment
Infectious Diseases | Per rehab facility | Complete antibiotic course
Cardiac Rehabilitation (Phase II) | After rehab discharge | Outpatient exercise program
Primary Care | After rehab discharge | Overall care, diabetes management
Hematology / Anticoagulation | 1-2 weeks | DVT anticoagulation management
When to Get Help Immediately

sternal wound problems (redness, drainage, opening, or fever), leg swelling or pain, bleeding, or signs of stroke.

Side Effects Kidney injury (monitored daily); rash if given too fast (Red Man Syndrome).
Monitoring Daily labs; infuse slowly over at least 60 minutes.
Teach-Back Family able to state purpose; instructed to report rash or skin flushing.
Piperacillin-tazobactam (Zosyn)
Purpose Broad-spectrum antibiotic targeting pneumonia and gram-negative bacteria.
Dose & Route 4.5 g IV every 6 hours, extended infusion over 3 hours.
Side Effects Diarrhea; low potassium; allergic reaction (report rash immediately).
Monitoring Renal function, electrolytes daily.
Teach-Back Teach-back deferred - patient sedated. Education provided to son.
Pantoprazole (Protonix)
Purpose Protects the stomach lining while on stress-ulcer prophylaxis.
Dose & Route 40 mg IV once daily, transitioning to oral when tolerating feeds.
Side Effects Low magnesium with long-term use (monitored); headache.

Purpose Blood thinner to prevent blood clots (DVT) in legs and lungs.

Purpose Controls blood sugar (glucose) which rises during critical illness.

Low blood sugar (hypoglycemia): sweating, confusion, shakiness.
Monitoring Point-of-care glucose every 1-2 hours while on infusion.
Teach-Back Patient able to describe symptoms of low blood sugar at discharge planning.

Purpose Corrects and prevents rapid irregular heartbeat (atrial fibrillation).
Dose & Route IV load then oral maintenance; dose adjusted per response.
Side Effects Thyroid problems, lung toxicity, liver effects (all monitored). Sensitivity to sunlight - use
sunscreen.
Monitoring Thyroid/liver labs monthly; chest X-ray annually; QT interval on ECG.
Teach-Back Family verbalized that patient needs ongoing monitoring after discharge. Written materials

Purpose Blood thinner for catheter-associated DVT (blood clot in neck vein).

judge_messages.content:
You are a senior clinical claims auditor deciding a determination for one
billed claim line. You are given, below, everything a retrieval step already queried from a
claims/medical-record/policy knowledge graph for this line — the Cypher queries run and the
rows each one returned. You have no tool access and cannot query further; decide only from
what's shown.

Domain knowledge for this review type:

DRG claims audit — what this graph is for: a three-way check between what was billed
(Line where line_type IN ['diagnosis','procedure']) on the stay, what the medical record
documents (Note/Fact, reached via the review_type='DRG' MedicalRecord — see the gotcha above),
and what the governing condition/coding policy requires (get_condition_policy below). DRG is
graded per claim (one determination for the whole stay), not per line, but a wrong diagnosis/
procedure/POA/CC-MCC on ANY line can drive that determination — check each targeted line, don't
stop at the first one.

Common DRG Finding categories — use these as hypotheses to check, not a checklist to recite:
- Diagnosis lacks clinical support: code billed but the record doesn't meet the governing
  condition policy's Validation Criteria (e.g. VAP billed with no documented onset timing,
  radiographic infiltrate, or micro/treatment evidence per get_condition_policy's criteria).
  Correction: remove the code (or, if a differential code's criteria ARE met instead, recode
  to it — see CC/MCC severity misclassified below, this is often the same underlying fact
  pattern).
- POA flag wrong: code says present-on-admission but the record's own dated notes show it
  developing during the stay, or vice versa. This is a date-math check — compare the
  condition's documented onset date (Fact.printed_date / Note.note_date) against
  Claim.claim_admit_date — not a keyword search.
- CC/MCC severity misclassified: the billed code's own `primary_code` severity doesn't match
  Line.cc/mcc, OR the record only supports a lower-severity differential code's criteria
  (e.g. J18.9 [CC] documented, not the [MCC] J95.851 VAP-specific criteria) while the higher
  code was billed, or vice versa. Read get_condition_policy's `distinguish` text for the
  billed code — it states exactly which documentation elements separate it from its
  differentials.
- Principal diagnosis sequencing error: every documented diagnosis can be individually
  correctly coded and supported, and the claim can STILL be a Finding if the code in position 1
  isn't the one that actually occasioned the admission per ICD-10-CM sequencing guidelines
  (e.g. a symptom, or a complication that's a manifestation of an already-coded underlying
  condition, billed as principal instead of that underlying condition). Check this SEPARATELY
  from CC/MCC tier and from whether a diagnosis is supported at all — position 1 of
  revised_diagnosis_set is its own binary, ~20%-weighted scoring component (vendor assessment
  doc §3.1.e), distinct from the "Remaining Codes" presence-match component.
- Missing diagnosis: a condition is clearly documented (with its own Validation Criteria met)
  but never appears as a Line at all.
- Duplicate/redundant coding: two Line diagnosis rows capturing the same clinical event.
- Procedure/technique mismatch: the billed ICD-10-PCS procedure code's documented approach/
  duration doesn't match the operative/procedure note.
- Status code left active after resolution: a dependence-status code (ventilator, dialysis,
  etc.) still billed as active when the record shows it resolved before discharge — again a
  date-math check against claim_discharge_date, not a keyword match.
- Missing procedure code: a performed procedure (e.g. "Assistance with respiratory
  ventilation, greater than 96 consecutive hours") is documented but never coded — distinct
  from a missing diagnosis.

Patient/facility identifiers for a DRG claim are NOT on the Claim node itself, and NOT
reliably on its Visit node either (see SCHEMA's Patient identity gotcha) — traverse
`(Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(Claim)` to get them, or, for MR_01..MR_10 only,
look them up on the paired readmission claim.

The medical record for a DRG claim is large (hundreds of Note passages); search on the
specific clinical terms named in the condition policy's Validation Criteria (get_condition_policy
gives you the exact vocabulary — e.g. "endotracheal", "purulent", "PaO2/FiO2") rather than a
generic term.

discharge_disposition (a separate required output field, not one of the Finding categories

Interpreter not\nrequired (English).\nNorepinephrine (Levophed)\nPurpose Raises blood pressure when the body is in shock.\nDose & Route Titrated via IV infusion to maintain blood pressure.\nSide Effects Decreased blood flow to hands/feet; irregular heartbeat.\nMonitoring Continuous blood pressure and heart rate monitoring.\nTeach-Back Family verbalized understanding that the medicine keeps blood pressure safe.\nVancomycin\nPurpose Antibiotic to treat the blood infection (sepsis) and potential MRSA.\nDose & Route Individualized IV dosing based on kidney function and blood levels.\nSide Effects Kidney injury (monitored daily); rash if given too fast (Red Man Syndrome).\nMonitoring Daily labs; infuse slowly over at least 60 minutes.\nTeach-Back Family able to state purpose; instructed to report rash or skin flushing.\nPiperacillin-tazobactam (Zosyn)\nPurpose Broad-spectrum antibiotic targeting pneumonia and gram-negative bacteria.\nDose & Route 4.5 g IV every 6 hours, extended infusion over 3 hours.\nSide Effects Diarrhea; low potassium; allergic reaction (report rash immediately).\nMonitoring Renal function, electrolytes daily.\nTeach-Back Teach-back deferred - patient sedated. Education provided to son.\nPantoprazole (Protonix)\nPurpose Protects the stomach lining while on stress-ulcer prophylaxis.\nDose & Route 40 mg IV once daily, transitioning to oral when tolerating feeds.\nSide Effects Low magnesium with long-term use (monitored); headache.\nMonitoring Magnesium levels weekly; discontinue at discharge if no indication.\nTeach-Back Patient verbalized that medication protects the stomach.\nEnoxaparin (Lovenox)\nPurpose Blood thinner to prevent blood clots (DVT) in legs and lungs.\nDose & Route Prophylactic dose; adjusted if active clot is confirmed.\nSide Effects Bruising at injection site; bleeding (report blood in urine/stool).\n[p.593] Monitoring Daily CBC; watch for signs of bleeding.\nTeach-Back Son acknowledged understanding of clot-prevention purpose and verbalized when to call\nfor help (unusual bleeding).\nInsulin infusion / Sliding scale\nPurpose Controls blood sugar (glucose) which rises during critical illness.\nDose & Route IV infusion titrated to glucose 140-180 mg/dL; transitioned to SC at recovery.\nSide Effects\nLow blood sugar (hypoglycemia): sweating, confusion, shakiness.\nMonitoring Point-of-care glucose every 1-2 hours while on infusion.\nTeach-Back Patient able to describe symptoms of low blood sugar at discharge planning.\nAmiodarone\nPurpose Corrects and prevents rapid irregular heartbeat (atrial fibrillation).\nDose & Route IV load then oral maintenance; dose adjusted per response.\nSide Effects Thyroid problems, lung toxicity, liver effects (all monitored). Sensitivity to sunlight - use\nsunscreen.\nMonitoring Thyroid/liver labs monthly; chest X-ray annually; QT interval on ECG.\nTeach-Back Family verbalized that patient needs ongoing monitoring after discharge. Written materials\nprovided.\nApixaban (Eliquis) - at discharge\nPurpose Blood thinner for catheter-associated DVT (blood clot in neck vein).\nDose & Route 10 mg twice daily x 7 days, then 5 mg twice daily x at least 3 months.\nSide Effects Increased bleeding risk - avoid NSAIDs, aspirin without physician approval.\nMonitoring No routine lab monitoring required, but report unusual bleeding.\nTeach-Back Patient and son demonstrated understanding of dose schedule and verbalized to avoid\nibuprofen. result.system_note: Audit summary and line-by-line determination for claim MR_10 (admit 2026-04-15 -> discharge 2026-08-15). I reviewed the billed diagnosis and procedure lines against the medical record notes and the governing DRG policies retrieved for cardiogenic shock, acute respiratory failure, AKI and sepsis. Key facts from the record that drive the determination: 1) Principal diagnosis (I21.09) - supported as principal. The admitting H&P and discharge/transfer documentation state acute anterior ST-elevation MI as the reason for admission and the team performed urgent coronary reperfusion and later emergency CABG (principal diagnosis sequencing is correct). Evidence: H&P assessment documents acute anterior STEMI with cardiogenic shock (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n9, History & Physical, p.668) and the operative/transfer course documents emergency 3-vessel CABG (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n1052, Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.936). See evidence_cited ev1 and ev4. 2) Cardiogenic shock (R57.0) - supported; meets the policy's documentation + device/management presumption. The record documents cardiogenic shock on admission, persistent hemodynamic instability, and placement of mechanical circulatory support (Impella CP and IABP). Per the cardiogenic shock policy, placement of MCS with provider attribution satisfies Criterion 2 for R57.0. Evidence: H&P and Interventional note (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n9, H&P, p.668; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n12, Interventional Cardiology Consultation, p.568) (ev1, ev2). 3) Acute respiratory failure (J96.01) - supported and documented on admission with objective hypoxemia and escalation to invasive ventilation. Admission ABG shows PaO2 62 on high-flow NRB and the record documents intubation for pulmonary edema; the presumption rule for invasive ventilation supports J96.01 even if a pre-intubation room-air ABG is unavailable. Evidence: ABG on admission (PaO2 62) (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n9, H&P, p.668) and the discharge note describing intubation and subsequent failed extubation/reintubation (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n1052, Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.936) (ev3, ev5). 4) Cardiac arrest (I46.9) - supported as a diagnosis but POA flag is incorrect on the billed claim. The medical record documents a pulseless ventricular tachycardia arrest that occurred on ICU day 4 (i.e., after admission), not present on arrival; therefore the POA indicator for I46.9 should be N, not Y. Evidence: discharge hospital course documenting pulseless ventricular tachycardia arrest on ICU day 4 with ROSC (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n1052, Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.936) (ev13). 5) Acute kidney injury (N17.9) - supported as an acute, post-contrast AKI (KDIGO stage 2) in the setting of cardiogenic shock, documented by nephrology; POA=N is correct. Nephrology documents contrast-induced KDIGO stage 2 AKI with creatinine peak ~2.8 and oliguric interval; discharge labs show renal recovery (creatinine 1.11 mg/dL). Per the AKI policy, this meets the Medical/Surgical and Acute-on-Chronic pathways when documented and substantiated by KDIGO criteria and nephrology assessment. Evidence: Nephrology consultation (KDIGO stage 2 AKI, creatinine peak 2.8) and discharge BMP showing creatinine 1.11 mg/dL (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n30, Nephrology Consultation, p.351; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n1052, Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.936) (ev6, ev7). 6) Sepsis (A41.9) - NOT supported as billed. The DRG sepsis policy requires provider documentation of sepsis (or clear objective criteria plus provider attribution) to code A41.9/A40.-. In this record I found documentation of a superficial sternal wound infection due to MSSA treated with cefazolin and a wound VAC, but I did not find a provider-authored diagnosis line explicitly documenting 'sepsis' as a confirmed diagnosis in the notes or the discharge/transfer diagnosis list. The discharge/transfer diagnoses enumerate wound infection, DVT, AKI, cardiogenic shock and related problems but do not list 'sepsis' as a discharge diagnosis; because policy requires provider documentation (or the sepsis clinical pathways with vasopressor + lactate etc.), A41.9 as billed (POA=Y, MCC) is not supported and is removed. Evidence: discharge/transfer summary problem list and the wound-infection description (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n1052, Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.936; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n1052, Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.936) (ev4, ev8). Note: there are antibiotic/education notes that reference 'sepsis' in lay terms (patient education) but those do not substitute for provider diagnosis documentation per policy. 7) Hypertensive CKD with ESRD (I12.0) - NOT supported. The record documents a contrast-induced AKI with recovery and nephrology explicitly anticipating recovery without RRT; there is no supporting provider documentation of stage 5 CKD/ESRD requiring I12.0. Discharge labs show creatinine recovery (creatinine 1.11 mg/dL). Per the AKI policy and Excludes1 rules, N17.x and N18.6 (ESRD) cannot be coded together without explicit documentation. I12.0 (hypertensive CKD stage 5/ESRD) is therefore not supported and is removed. Evidence: Nephrology consult documenting contrast-induced KDIGO 2 AKI, creatinine trends and recovery, and discharge BMP with creatinine 1.11 mg/dL (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n30, Nephrology Consultation, p.351; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n1052, Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.936) (ev6, ev7). 8) Procedure coding and laterality conflict (06BQ0ZZ) - human escalation required. The claim contains ICD-10-PCS 06BQ0ZZ (Excision of right saphenous vein, open approach). The operative/procedure narrative(s) retrieved include explicit language that a saphenous vein was harvested from the left leg for SVGs (see the operative/procedure note excerpts in the retrieval transcript). The dataset's conflict-tracking flags these particular procedure-note passages as a record_vs_claim conflict (CONFLICT-00070 / CONFLICT-00279), indicating the record and the billed line cannot both be correct and the record does not settle which is right. Because laterality drives ICD-10-PCS assignment and the record passages conflict, this specific procedure line needs human review to resolve laterality. I therefore mark the claim Finding and request HITL for the 06BQ0ZZ laterality. Evidence: discharge summary documents 3-vessel CABG with SVGs (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n1052, Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.936) and the separate procedure note(s) (conflicted) describing left-leg harvest (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n60 / NOTE-Readmission-RM_10-index-MR_10.pdf-n55 - flagged in the conflict list). See hitl_question for details. Net effect and corrective actions taken in this audit (claim-level): - Removed I12.0 (hypertensive CKD stage 5 / ESRD) - unsupported; evidence shows contrast-induced AKI with recovery and no RRT (ev6, ev7). - Removed A41.9 (sepsis, unspecified) - no provider-authored sepsis diagnosis found in the chart or discharge problem list; only wound infection (MSSA) documented (ev4, ev8). If the provider has separate documentation explicitly diagnosing sepsis (with vasopressor/lactate or statement 'sepsis'), supply it for reconsideration. - Changed POA for I46.9 (cardiac arrest) from Y to N - arrest occurred on ICU day 4 per hospital course (ev13). - Left all other billed diagnoses and procedures in place pending resolution of the laterality conflict for saphenous vein excision (06BQ0ZZ) - see HITL request. Supported high-severity MCC diagnoses (R57.0, J96.01, I50.23) remain billed because provider documentation and objective data or device placement meet the policy validation criteria (ev1, ev2, ev3, ev12, ev11). Documents and quotations relied upon (see evidence_cited entries below) - cited passages are from: H&P (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n9, p.668), Interventional Cardiology consult (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n12, p.568), Nephrology consult (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n30, p.351), and Discharge / Transfer Summary (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n1052, pp.936-937) among others. The cardiogenic shock and respiratory-failure policies were applied as retrieved during the review (policy rule excerpts for R57.0 and J96.01 guided the validation criteria used above). Reviewer conclusion: Finding. The claim contains unsupported/miscoded diagnoses (I12.0 and A41.9 removed) and an incorrect POA flag (I46.9 changed to POA=N). Additionally, a procedure-laterality conflict for 06BQ0ZZ requires human resolution before final procedural coding can be certified. See code_decisions, revised_diagnosis_set, revised_procedure_set and hitl_question for specifics.
result.rationale_letter: To: Coding and Medical Records Department Re: Audit determination - Inpatient claim MR_10 (Admit 04/15/2026 - Discharge 08/15/2026) We audited the full DRG-level coding for the above inpatient stay against the medical record and applicable DRG validation criteria. After review, we find the claim contains multiple supported high-severity diagnoses (acute anterior STEMI, cardiogenic shock, acute respiratory failure, AKI, cardiac arrest, post-operative complications) but also contains diagnostic entries that are not supported by the provider documentation and at least one POA flag that is incorrect. The audit changes are listed below with the factual basis. Audit findings and corrections made: 1) I21.09 (ST-elevation myocardial infarction) - retained and remains the principal diagnosis. The H&P and discharge/transfer summary document acute anterior STEMI as the reason for admission and subsequent emergency CABG (source: H&P 04/15/2026 and Discharge/Transfer Summary, Dr. Menon) (supporting documentation available in the chart). 2) R57.0 (Cardiogenic shock) - retained (MCC). Provider documentation and placement of mechanical circulatory support (Impella CP and IABP) for cardiogenic shock satisfy the policy validation criteria for cardiogenic shock (policy presumption rule for MCS placement) and justify MCC assignment. 3) J96.01 (Acute respiratory failure with hypoxia) - retained (MCC). Objective hypoxemia and initiation of invasive ventilation are documented; the clinical intervention requirements for validation are met. 4) I46.9 (Cardiac arrest) - retained but POA changed to N. The chart documents pulseless VT arrest on ICU day 4 with ROSC; this event occurred after admission and therefore should not be indicated Present-on-Admission (POA=Y). The POA indicator on the submitted claim is incorrect. 5) N17.9 (Acute kidney failure) - retained (CC) with POA=N. Nephrology documents KDIGO stage 2 post-contrast AKI with a creatinine peak and subsequent recovery; acute AKI coding is supported. 6) A41.9 (Sepsis, unspecified organism) - REMOVED. The DRG sepsis policy requires explicit provider documentation of sepsis or the combination of specific sepsis criteria with provider attribution. The chart documents a superficial sternal wound infection due to MSSA and antibiotic therapy, but I found no provider-authored documentation of 'sepsis' as a confirmed diagnosis in the progress notes or discharge/transfer problem list. Without provider documentation or clear septic-shock criteria attributed to infection in the chart, A41.9 is not supported and is removed from the claim. If the provider can supply contemporaneous documentation explicitly diagnosing sepsis (or documentation of vasopressor-dependent shock + lactate >2 attributed to infection), we will re-evaluate. 7) I12.0 (Hypertensive CKD with stage 5 CKD / ESRD) - REMOVED. The nephrology consult and discharge labs document a contrast-induced AKI with recovery and state no RRT was anticipated; there is no evidence of ESRD or documented stage 5 CKD in the record to justify I12.0. Accordingly, I12.0 is not supportable for this encounter and is removed. 8) Procedure-laterality conflict (06BQ0ZZ - excision of right saphenous vein): The operative/procedure documentation retrieved in the chart contains conflicting laterality statements relative to the billed code (notes describing left-leg SVG harvest vs. a claim line for right saphenous excision). Because laterality is determinative for ICD-10-PCS assignment and the record contains a documented conflict that the automated review cannot resolve, this item is referred for human review. Please reconcile the operative note(s) and supply the final operative record specifying the harvested vein laterality so we can finalize the ICD-10-PCS assignment for the saphenous-vein harvest procedure. Corrective action requested from provider / coding team: - Confirm and provide any provider-authored documentation that explicitly diagnoses sepsis (or confirm absence). If sepsis was documented, provide the note(s) so A41.9 can be reinstated if supported. - Confirm whether the patient has ESRD or documented CKD stage 5 that was present on admission; if so, provide documentation. Otherwise I12.0 will remain removed. - Reconcile the operative/procedure documentation to confirm which saphenous vein (right vs left) was harvested for SVG grafting so the PCS procedure can be coded to the correct laterality. Enclosed: (1) The audit's revised diagnosis list and procedure list; (2) evidence citations from the chart used to support each correction. Sincerely, Senior Clinical Claims Auditor

code_decisions.reason: Admission ABG with PaO2 62 on high-flow oxygen and documentation of intubation and mechanical ventilation satisfies policy criteria and the presumption rule for invasive ventilation.
Cardiac arrest documented on ICU day 4 (post-admission); POA should be 'N'.
Nephrology documents KDIGO stage 2 contrast-induced AKI with creatinine peak and subsequent recovery; POA=N is correct.
Post-cardiotomy atrial fibrillation is documented as a postoperative complication; POA=N is supported by the discharge course.
Post-operative complication coding supported by post-op course; retained as complication-of-procedure documentation.
Superficial sternal wound infection after surgery is documented (MSSA) and justifies an infection-following-procedure code.
Provider links MSSA organism to the documented sternal wound infection; organism-specific causal code supported.
Discharge summary documents right popliteal DVT treated with apixaban.
Residual multivessel coronary disease documented on cath/consultation supports chronic ischemic heart disease coding.
Admission hyperglycemia and inpatient insulin management documented; diabetes with hyperglycemia supported.
Longstanding hypertension documented in past medical history.
History of hyperlipidemia documented in problem list/PMH.

Facesheet and discharge documentation indicate full-code status and the discharge/transfer summary does not document Do-Not-Resuscitate; Z66 (Do not resuscitate) is not supported by the chart documentation.
No provider documentation of ESRD or CKD stage 5; nephrology documents contrast-induced AKI with recovery and no RRT. I12.0 (hypertensive CKD stage 5/ESRD) is not supported.

Provider-authored diagnosis of 'sepsis' is not present in the chart or discharge problem list; the record documents a localized post-operative MSSA sternal wound infection but no documented sepsis syndrome meeting the policy requirement for A41.9 as coded.
Primary PCI to proximal LAD documented (TIMI 2 flow) supports the percutaneous dilation with DES code.
Impella CP placement documented for cardiogenic shock supports the MCS insertion code.
Intra-aortic balloon pump placement documented supports the intraluminal aortic device code.
Emergency CABG (LIMA to LAD plus vein grafts) documented; the one-site bypass PCS is retained as part of the coded multi-graft set.
Emergency 3-vessel CABG documented; the two-site bypass PCS plus the one-site PCS together represent the three grafts performed.
